chunks.label: Shops and parks
chunks.rationale: Lets you say where you're popping out to nearby.
chunks.interference: Omise covers restaurants and bars too, not just shops.

chunks.label: From place to world
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about where things are, from one spot to the whole world.
chunks.interference: Sekai is the world; sekaijuu means all over it.

chunks.label: Home and neighbours
chunks.rationale: Lets you say where you live and refer politely to other people's homes.
chunks.interference: Manshon is any apartment block, not a mansion; otaku (your home) sounds like otaku (geek).

chunks.label: School stages
chunks.rationale: Lets you place memories by school stage, from primary to high school.
chunks.interference: Chuugaku is middle school and koukou is high school; they're easy to swap.

chunks.label: Meeting new people
chunks.rationale: Lets you introduce yourself, say where you're from and swap contacts.
chunks.interference: Shusshin is where you're from; jimoto is where you grew up or live now.

chunks.label: Chatting and topics
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about chatting and what to talk about.
chunks.interference: Neta is something to talk about; wadai is the topic itself.

chunks.label: Replies and reactions
chunks.rationale: Lets you say whether someone answered and how they reacted.
chunks.interference: Henji is any reply; henshin is only a reply to a message.

chunks.label: Information and secrets
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about things you find out, read, keep track of or keep quiet.

chunks.label: Right, wrong, opposite
chunks.rationale: Lets you call something a mistake, the right call, or the other way round.
chunks.interference: Gyaku is just the reverse; hantai also means being against something.

chunks.label: Opinions and excuses
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask for views, give advice and push back on excuses.
chunks.interference: Iken is your view; tachiba is the position you're in.

chunks.label: Worth and purpose
chunks.rationale: Lets you say whether something is worth doing, or that you've got something on.
chunks.interference: You in you ga aru means business or an errand, not use.

chunks.label: Trouble and limits
chunks.rationale: Lets you apologise for trouble and say you've had enough.
chunks.interference: Toraburu is something going wrong; meiwaku is trouble you cause someone.

chunks.label: Cause and effect
chunks.rationale: Lets you say what caused something and what it led to.
chunks.interference: Gen'in is the cause of a problem; kikkake is what got something started.

chunks.label: Goals and plans
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about what you're aiming for and what comes first.
chunks.interference: Mokuteki is the purpose; mokuhyou is the target you aim to hit.

chunks.label: Basics and conditions
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk through what something involves and choose between options.
chunks.interference: Jouken means terms, not physical condition.

chunks.label: Impressions and behaviour
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe how someone comes across, acts and is treated.
chunks.interference: Imeeji is an impression in your mind, not a photo.

chunks.label: How things unfold
chunks.rationale: Lets you tell how a situation went and where it stands now.
chunks.interference: Nagare is the general flow; tenkai is a twist or turn in it.
